outroLine: Prove the route before it matters.

beats.shot: Land on the Delivery tab: protocol rail (HTTP, SFTP, FTPS, Email, Erply ERP, Directo ERP) with HTTP selected; cursor walks the protocol cards.
beats.vo: Delivery is the last leg — how a finished order physically reaches this supplier. Pick the channel they want. A direct H T T P endpoint, S F T P, email, or straight into an E R P like Erply or Directo.

beats.shot: Cursor opens the Output format select and picks CSV; the 'auto-transforms into this format' note sits underneath.
beats.vo: Then the output format their system expects. Once it's set, every order to this supplier is transformed into exactly this format before it's sent.

beats.shot: Cursor clicks the Endpoint URL field and types the supplier's order endpoint; then opens Auth type and picks API key.
beats.vo: Point it at their endpoint, and pick the authentication their side needs. A P I key, bearer token, basic auth, or O Auth 2.

beats.shot: Cursor rests on the 'Delivery state boundary' card: transform creates an artifact; only this delivery workflow can mark it delivered.
beats.vo: Notice the boundary ProcuLink draws here. Transforming an order only creates the file. Nothing is ever marked delivered until this delivery workflow actually delivers it.

beats.shot: Cursor moves to the Test-fire button in the footer and rests on it (config not saved in the demo, so it is not fired).
beats.vo: Before any real order rides this route, you test-fire it — a safe test payload to the endpoint. And be precise about what a green result means. The endpoint answered. That is not the same as the supplier accepting an order, and ProcuLink never pretends it is.

beats.shot: Cursor clicks the Auto-deliver checkbox in the panel header; it ticks on.
beats.vo: And when the route has earned your trust, auto-deliver sends ready orders without the manual step. Until then, every send stays a human decision.
